annotations.text:
Three ways to route visitors from the MHLC landing page into the rest of the site.

All three replace the section that currently sits under the hero. The global nav bar stays identical to the secondary pages in every option — this device lives in the page body, so the homepage can speak in the visitor's voice without breaking the site's navigation.

Every link points at a destination that already exists.

Each concept explores a different axis, not three shades of one idea:

A — spatial metaphor. Navigation drawn as a garden path.
B — conversational. The visitor completes a sentence about themselves.
C — structural. The page forks into two honest halves.

B's chips work — click them. A and C are static.

A — THE PATH

Why: the project's whole thesis is paths, gardens and walking rather than corridors. Navigation that IS a path is the most on-brand device available and unmistakably theirs. Six audiences, no interaction cost, reads top to bottom.

Tradeoff: the illustration has to stay this restrained or it turns twee. It is the safest of the three and the least surprising.

B — FINISH THE SENTENCE

Why: speaks in the visitor's voice instead of the institution's, and turns a nav problem into a human sentence. One click, nothing leaves the page, and the panel can hold richer content than a row.

Tradeoff: needs JavaScript (all four panels must render without it), and four options is the ceiling before it stops reading as a sentence — so clinicians and region get folded into 'my work' and 'my community'.

C — TWO WAYS IN

Why: zero reading required to self-select, and it is honest that this site does two very different jobs. Strongest of the three for donors, who currently scroll past family content to reach anything for them. Stacks to mobile unchanged.

Tradeoff: six audiences collapse to two. The hard visual split could read as a divide rather than one community — the line underneath is there to soften it.
